subject: Hosted API: sustained p95 elevation — AlphaHealth status update
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harris <ben.harris@alphahealth.com>, AlphaHealth Support <support@alphahealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API: sustained p95 elevation — AlphaHealth status update

Hi Ben / AlphaHealth team,

Quick status from Redwood: starting ~08:45 PST we observed a sustained elevation in p95 latencies for generation endpoints serving your account (route: /v1/generate). The effect is partial — not all requests error, but customers are seeing intermittent 10–25% higher tail latency for conversations with long context (>1k tokens).

What were doing now:
- Activated dimmer policy at 09:00 PST for non-critical dev keys to reduce pressure on shared pools.
- Rerouting a portion of traffic to warm dedicated pools that are compatible with your pinned model.
- Ops has captured a timeline and p95 traces; attaching a short CSV (alpha_incident_timeline_20261125.csv) and a log snapshot.

Impact to AlphaHealth: we expect increased p95 for some requests and occasional retries from your client. No request-level errors have been observed at scale (HTTP 5xx rate remains within baseline), but latency may affect user-facing flows.

ETA: our initial mitigation reduces tail within ~30–45 minutes; we will update you with confirmed recovery or next steps in 1 hour.

If you have live jobs you want us to deprioritize or to temporarily exclude from rebalancing, reply with job ids and we can pin them to dedicated capacity.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is time-sensitive. Ill keep you posted.

—Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
(attachment: alpha_incident_timeline_20261125.csv)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harris <ben.harris@alphahealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:05:30 -0800
Subject: RE: Hosted API: sustained p95 elevation — AlphaHealth status update

Ben — quick technical update from the ops team (ETA/next actions):

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
- We observed KV-cache hotspotting on a small subset of prefix buckets tied to longer-context request patterns. The hot buckets triggered local backpressure and slowed KV fetches on the inference path, which manifests as elevated p95 for sequences >1k tokens.
- Because your workload uses a few high-entropy prefixes (customer summaries + large policy docs), you were disproportionately affected.

What we've done so far:
- Rebalanced the hot KV shards across additional hosts (09:32–09:48 PST).
- Temporarily increased the prefix cache TTL for affected pools to reduce repeated miss churn.
- Enabled a targeted rolling restart of 6 worker processes in the warm dedicated pool to flush contested state (09:50–10:02 PST).

Observed effect:
- P95 improved by ~35% for the rerouted traffic within 12 minutes after rollouts; aggregate p95 for AlphaHealth decreased but remains ~10% above baseline for some long-context flows.
- No increase in 5xxs. Token accounting unaffected.

Next steps (today):
- Continue gradual shard rebalancing; finish by 13:00 PST.
- Run backfill of prefix cache metrics and a focused regression test for your most common prompt shapes.
- Produce a short incident timeline and log snapshot (attached: ops_snapshot_p95_logs.txt).

If you can pause the scheduled batches you mentioned, that will help accelerate recovery for live traffic. We will not bill duplicate tokens for server-side retries originating from our retry policy during the mitigation window — we will itemize this in the post-incident summary.

Ill follow up in an hour with updated p95 numbers and a recovery confirmation.

—Evelyn Hart
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
(evelyn_hart@redwood.com)
(attachment: ops_snapshot_p95_logs.txt)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Hosted API: sustained p95 elevation — AlphaHealth status update (resolved)

Hi Ben — final update and next steps.

Status: Resolved as of 14:58 PST on 2026-11-26. The shard rebalancing and targeted restarts completed; tail latency for your production keys is back within SLA (p95 within 5% of baseline across monitored routes). We closed the active mitigation and rolled dimmer back where appropriate.

Post-incident summary: we published a short postmortem and a timeline to our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RSW-6125. Summary highlights: KV prefix hotspotting → shard imbalance → elevated p95 for long-context requests. The full postmortem will add long-term mitigations (fine-grained shard auto-scaling, earlier hotspot detection via prefix-entropy signals).

Billing: as Evelyn noted, we will not charge for duplicated tokens caused by our server-side retries during the mitigation window (2026-11-25 08:45 PST to 2026-11-26 14:58 PST). I will follow up with a line-item credit; youll see a HubSpot ticket for the credit (HS-34567).

Next: Kimberly and I (Marcus) would like to schedule a 30-minute technical review with your infra team to walk through the timeline and planned mitigations. Proposed slots: Mon 11/30 10:00–11:00 PST or Tue 12/1 08:00–08:30 PST. Please let us know what works.

Apologies again for the disruption — we understand the impact and appreciate your partnership while we resolved it.

—Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
(links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RSW-6125)
